bio:
His kinship to John no longer depends on the Topping route. The Woodhull Genealogy ([R4-S1]) makes him the son of Richard Woodhull IV (1712-1788) and Margaret Smith (1714-1803), 'daughter of Edmund Smith of the "Bull Smith" family, and Susannah Floyd'. Pelletreau ([R4-S2]) and Thompson ([R4-S3]) both give Edmund Smith 1st as the only son of Adam Smith, son of the patentee, and list Margaret (wife of Richard Woodhull) among Edmund's children; Edmund's 1734 will names daughters Anne and Margaret. Path: Bull Smith -> Adam -> Edmund 1st -> Margaret -> Abraham, 4 generations below John's 11th-great-grandparents Bull Smith & Sarah Hammond: 3rd cousin 8 times removed. His wife Mary Smith was herself a Bull Smith descendant through both parents (Obadiah, son of Daniel 2d; Anna, daughter of Edmund 1st by his second wife Mary), so Abraham married his half-first cousin.

The Topping route is now doubtful: the Woodhull Genealogy says his great-grandmother Temperance, wife of Richard Woodhull II, was a daughter of Rev. Jonah Fordham, while Southampton records record Richard's 1684 marriage to 'Temperance Topping'. Howell's Topping genealogy gives Capt. Thomas Topping no daughter Temperance. The likeliest reading is that she was Temperance Fordham, widow of a Topping, which would leave the Woodhulls with no Topping blood.
funFacts: George Washington suggested his alias 'Samuel Culper', a play on Culpeper County, Virginia.
